predictions: The lipid associations and expression associations may arise from linkage to another causal change or a mechanism that does not involve altered TF binding at this base.

chains.title: FOXA1-mediated regulation of SORT1
chains.cell_type: Liver; the relevant cell type is not resolved

links.claim: FOXA1 occupies the variant in HepG2 and is expressed in the stated liver cancer cell context. FOXA1 is a reasonable lead among the listed liver-context factors because it has more reported HepG2 peaks here than FOXA2 and is more highly expressed in the stated context; this does not establish that it is causal. Alt (T) is the working prediction for stronger binding, not a direction supported by allele-specific evidence: no QBiC-SELEX result is supplied.
The variant lies in enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1374646, but the reported activity maxima do not establish activity in liver cells.

SORT1 is a plausible target: it has a high locus-to-gene score and the T allele is associated with higher SORT1 expression in bulk liver. These data do not demonstrate that this cCRE or FOXA1 causes the expression association.
A liver-context mechanism is plausible from FOXA1 occupancy in HepG2 and the bulk-liver SORT1 eQTL, but hepatocyte-specific enhancer activity or FOXA1 mediation is not established.

The variant is associated with cholesterol and LDL traits. Several reported associations list G as the effect allele, whereas T is associated with higher liver SORT1 expression; the evidence does not establish that this expression change mediates the lipid associations. Literature describes protective effects of hepatic expression of the gene cluster, not a FOXA1-mediated effect of this variant.

predictions: Precise G-to-T editing in an appropriate liver-cell model will change SORT1 expression in the direction suggested by the liver eQTL, and FOXA1 perturbation will attenuate that allele-dependent difference.
FOXA1 occupancy will be higher on T than G if the working binding-direction prediction is correct; the supplied evidence does not establish this direction.
falsified_if: Precise editing produces no reproducible SORT1 expression difference in a relevant liver-cell model.
The allele-dependent SORT1 difference persists unchanged after effective FOXA1 perturbation.

next_experiment: The cheapest informative first test is a paired G/T allele reporter assay in a liver-context cell line with and without FOXA1 depletion.
